entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abba Saul was a fourth generation Tanna and the leader of the Ebenezer community in the island of Efate during the late 17th century. He played a crucial role in the conversion of the island's population to Christianity, using the translation of the Bible into the local language of Efate to facilitate his mission. Abba Saul's work had significant consequences for the development of Christianity in the Pacific and its impact on the indigenous cultures of the region.

Abba Saul was born around 1650 and died in 1716. His legacy extends beyond his religious accomplishments, as he also played a key role in the early history of education on Efate, establishing schools and promoting literacy among the local population.

One striking statistic about Abba Saul's work is that he successfully translated the Bible into Efate within just two years, demonstrating his dedication to his mission and his ability to adapt to new cultural contexts.
